# Independent audit: disjoint residual-sector credits and the one-thirty-second bound

Audited `candidate cf1b9ba5ada0a5ef` in full and Section 8 of `candidate 6b20e938071f0379`, retaining the latter source's previously audited hypotheses and scalar parameters. **PASS**, with one harmless wording repair requested: an intersection of closed A with strict halfspaces is convex but need not be open in the ambient space. Its positive-volume interior exhaustion, which the proof actually uses, is valid.

The independent verifier `supporting computation verify_disjoint_unique_sector_credit_slab_recovery.py` passes **956 exact checks**, including actual rational polygon residuals, their midpoint sums, disjoint-sector area accounting, the algebra of (33), and the derivative and integer comparison in (37)--(38). These checks supplement the following proof audit; they do not establish any global criticality for the test polygons.

## 1. The common-body geometry in every dimension

For x in R_i and y in B, each j!=i satisfies v_j.(x+y)<0. Thus their actual midpoint belongs to K and its prescribed unique sector Z_i. If a point belonged to two distinct Z_i, every one of its d+1 normal coordinates would be negative, contradicting their zero sum. The sectors really are pairwise disjoint; no separate realizability assumption or independent choice of bodies is involved.

If |R_i|>0, it has an interior point p satisfying all the strict cuts. Its closure is a convex body of the same volume. The compact homothets p+(1-epsilon)(closure R_i-p) lie inside R_i, because their cut values are strict convex combinations with the values at p, and lie inside A by convexity. Apply ordinary Brunn--Minkowski to each such homothet and B. Their midpoint sums already lie in the original Z_i; taking only their numerical volumes to the limit proves (1) without requiring target-boundary convergence.

Every Z_i with i in J satisfies all cuts indexed outside J. Disjointness therefore proves (2), including the case of all indices, where the ambient target is K. The complement union bound proves (3). The planar critical identity (4) uses exactly the common actual mass Q and zero B capture, so the middle cap mass is Q-U_l. All continuous boundary lines are area-null.

## 2. Planar scalar elimination

The two actual residual bodies have lower areas rw and (r+y-1)w>0. Their disjoint midpoint sums give (32), retaining both square-root terms. Combining the already proved middle profile and target upper bound gives

    k-Q+u <= 5b/9+[(10r-7)/18-y]w.

Subtracting (32), dividing by b, and multiplying by 36 gives exactly (33). No swept-segment or injected reserve is added to this overlapping lower bound.

The retained range has 1/4<=r<175/256<1, 1-r<y<=1, and 0<x<(4/3)(175/256-r). In particular 5-2r+45y>50-47r>0, so substituting the lower bound z>=1/(32(r+x+y)) is legitimate under the assumed a/b>=1/32.

For fixed r,y, both resulting terms decrease when x increases. Enlarging x to x_bar is therefore a valid lower estimate. The first term then increases in y because its derivative numerator is 47r+45x_bar-5>0. For the square-root term, differentiation on t=r+y-1>0 gives the sign of 1+x_bar-sqrt(rt)>0; indeed 0<t<=r<1. Continuity permits t=0. Lowering y to 1-r thus leaves the one-variable lower bound f(r).

The exact derivative is

    32 A(r)^2 f'(r)=-1483/64+9(367/192)sqrt(32)sqrt(A(r)/r).

Here A(r)>1 and r<1, making the positive term greater than 45 while 1483/64<24. Thus f is strictly increasing. At r=1/4, it equals 153/202+18/sqrt(202)>2. The last inequality is equivalent to 18sqrt(202)>251, certified by 65448>63001. This contradicts (33) and proves a<b/32 in the stated two-positive-residual branch.

The conclusion retains every original branch hypothesis, including the actual proper-A, zero-B common critical circuit, B nonheavy, the target upper bound, and exactly three contributing fibers. It does not exclude the remaining positive small-A regime, give a numerical value to an unrelated compactness threshold, or prove OC in general.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
